scoreInfo.title: How the score works
scoreInfo.composition: Six domains (10 points each) plus enduring impact (40 points) make up a 100-point total. Where that total lands sets the rank.

domainQuestions.political: Did they change political systems, policy, or diplomatic order?
domainQuestions.strategic: Did they change military strategy, weapons, or security doctrine?
domainQuestions.tech: Did they advance technology or science?
domainQuestions.social: Did they change social norms, ethical debate, or institutions?
domainQuestions.economic: Did they change industrial structure or how economies work?
domainQuestions.cultural: Did they change currents or genres in culture and art?

scoreInfo.note: The highest scores go to what a figure did themselves; laying the groundwork a field could not have stood without comes next. Connections that only reach through several removes do not count.

transhistoricityInfo.title: Enduring Impact
transhistoricityInfo.definition: A 40-point measure of how far a figure's mark reaches beyond their own lifetime, across the span of human history.
transhistoricityInfo.criteria: Two things count: whether the influence held over a long stretch of time, and whether it settled into the foundations of civilization — religion, law, scientific principle — in a way that will carry forward. Unproven predictions about the future are left out.
